conventions.convention: For an n by p real matrix, S(X)=XᵀX/n; the empirical spectral distribution is normalized by p and counts eigenvalues with multiplicity. The smallest positive eigenvalue is defined only when a positive eigenvalue exists.
The Stieltjes transform is m(z)=∫(x−z)⁻¹ dμ(x), with Im z>0.
The aspect ratio is γ=p/n. The support endpoints are (1−√γ)² and (1+√γ)², and the zero atom has mass (1−1/γ)₊. The definition assumes Countable Choice.

The weak-law theorem assumes AC and a common probability space, with independent entries within each matrix and one common entry law across sizes; it does not require nested matrices or independence across sizes.
The edge results use upper-left blocks of one infinite iid array, with mean zero, variance one and finite fourth moment.

The Bai–Yin theorem counts zero singular values among min(n,pₙ) values away from aspect one. At aspect one it asserts convergence of the eventually defined smallest positive singular value, without asserting eventual full rank.

load_bearing.statement: For the centered slow truncations, oriented with mₕ rows and Nₕ columns and normalized by √Nₕ, almost surely limsupₕ ‖Tₕ,ℓ‖op ≤ (2ℓ+1)(ℓ+1)y^((ℓ−1)/2) for every fixed integer ℓ≥1. For the original nested iid finite-fourth-moment matrices, almost surely limsupₕ ‖Xₕ/√h‖op<∞.
For the stated nested iid finite-fourth-moment blocks, orient the matrix with mₕ=min(h,pₕ) rows and Nₕ=max(h,pₕ) columns, set Aₕ=Zₕ/√Nₕ and y=min(γ,γ⁻¹). Almost surely limsupₕ ‖AₕAₕᵀ−(1+y)I‖op≤2√y.

For the stated nested iid mean-zero variance-one finite-second-moment array, assuming an almost-sure finite coarse norm bound, n⁻¹Tr(Gₙᵏ) converges almost surely to Σₛ₌₁ᵏ k⁻¹ binom(k,s)binom(k,s−1)γˢ for each fixed k≥1. Positive eigenvalues exist eventually, liminf λmax(Gₙ)≥(1+√γ)² and limsup λmin⁺(Gₙ)≤(1−√γ)² almost surely.

For comparable rectangular blocks of one nested iid mean-zero variance-one finite-fourth-moment array, a deterministic slow truncation gives eventual entrywise equality almost surely, negligible mean-matrix norm, uniform row and column second-moment laws, a vanishing normalized maximum entry, a bounded normalized fourth-power sum, and vanishing Frobenius norms of the stated higher entry-power matrices.
Assume Countable Choice. For every γ>0, μγ is a Borel probability measure supported on [0,∞). Its transform satisfies 1+zmγ=mγ/(1+γmγ) and Im(1−γ−z−γzmγ)≤−Im z for Im z>0.

Under AC, the stated common-space independent-entry matrices with one common mean-zero variance-one finite-fourth-moment entry law and pₙ/n→γ∈(0,∞) have empirical spectral distributions converging weakly almost surely to the displayed Marchenko–Pastur density plus an atom (1−1/γ)₊ at zero.

For the stated nested iid finite-fourth-moment blocks, the smallest of min(n,pₙ) singular values divided by √n converges almost surely to 1−√γ when γ<1 and √γ−1 when γ>1, giving eventual full rectangular rank. When γ=1, the smallest positive singular value is eventually defined and its ratio to √n tends to zero.

concerns.concern: Fact F9 says 'Chebyshev's inequality bounds a deviation probability by variance divided by squared deviation' and cites thm-chebyshev-inequality; Step 5.1 applies it to Tₙ=(npₙ)⁻¹ΣXₙ,ij². The cited theorem is explicitly titled 'Chebyshev's inequality on a finite probability space' and states its claim for a 'finite real random variable', whose library definition has finite range. Tₙ need not have finite range. The displayed bound is correct and follows immediately by applying the general random-variable Markov inequality to (Tₙ−1)², but that derivation or an appropriately general supplier is missing.

The Definition says 'its total mass is established by the Marchenko–Pastur law below.' The current dedicated justification lem-marchenko-pastur-formula-defines-a-finite-measure already calculates total mass one independently, and the weak-law theorem then cites that lemma. This sentence describes the justification order inaccurately.
